hypothesis: V58's BTC configuration is formally bidirectional but operationally incomplete for bullish participation because its only executable long mechanism is a rare hourly downside-sweep reversal; a future successor must distinguish side authority from market-regime opportunity coverage.
decision: Classify the current BTC long as a selective reversal control, not general bullish coverage. Retain V58 unchanged while live ETH and SP500 capital remains open, do not restore the rejected BTC long families, and require any successor described as operationally bidirectional to include a separately validated bullish-continuation mechanism or explicitly disclose the missing continuation regime.
falsifier: Update this diagnosis if the frozen V58 audit is shown to contain an executable BTC continuation-long route, if an eligible BTC long was lost after signal generation rather than absent at the provider boundary, or if an independently preregistered continuation-long mechanism passes the stated functional, economic, execution, and shared-portfolio validation contract.

limitations: The ten all-live BTC-long lifecycles span multiple profile fingerprints and execution contracts; their pooled result is descriptive, not current-profile edge evidence.
Three BTC tuned-v2 Hulk longs are too few to estimate repeatability or $5,000-scale execution economics.
The closest historical Hulk-long family is not parameter-identical to a hypothetical robust-v3 long route.
Rejecting the exact historical families does not prove that no profitable BTC continuation-long mechanism exists.
No numeric trade-frequency requirement is inferred from operator frustration; it requires an explicit portfolio opportunity target or an empirically justified power/capacity design.
This record cannot pause, retune, route, size, enter, close, restart, or promote any live strategy or lifecycle.
